segments.speaker: MIA
segments.en: Hi, Rob. How’s the course going?

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: Oh, hi, Mia. Yeah, great. I can’t believe the first term’s nearly over.

segments.speaker: MIA
segments.en: I saw your group’s performance last night at the student theatre. It was good.

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: Really? Yeah ... but now we have to write a report on the whole thing, an in-depth analysis. I don’t know where to start. Like, I have to write about the role I played, the doctor, how I developed the character.

segments.speaker: MIA
segments.en: Well, what was your starting point?

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: Er ... my grandfather was a doctor before he retired, and I just based it on him.

segments.speaker: MIA
segments.en: OK, but how? Did you talk to him about it?

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: He must have all sorts of stories, but he never says much about his work, even now. He has a sort of authority though.

segments.speaker: MIA
segments.en: So how did you manage to capture that?

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: I’d ... I’d visualise what he must have been like in the past, when he was sitting in his consulting room listening to his patients. [[ ]]

segments.speaker: MIA
segments.en: OK, so that’s what you explain in your report.

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: Right.

segments.speaker: MIA
segments.en: Then there’s the issue of atmosphere – so in the first scene we needed to know how boring life was in the doctor’s village in the 1950s, so when the curtain went up on the first scene in the waiting room, there was that long silence before anyone spoke. And then people kept saying the same thing over and over, like ‘Cold, isn’t it?’ [[ ]]

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: Yes, and everyone wore grey and brown, and just sat in a row.

segments.speaker: MIA
segments.en: Yes, all those details of the production.

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: And I have to analyse how I functioned in the group – what I found out about myself. I know I was so frustrated at times, when we couldn’t agree.

segments.speaker: MIA
segments.en: Yes. So did one person emerge as the leader?

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: Sophia did. That was OK – she helped us work out exactly what to do, for the production. And that made me feel better, I suppose. [[ ]]

segments.speaker: MIA
segments.en: When you understood what needed doing?

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: Yes. And Sophia did some research, too. That was useful in developing our approach.

segments.speaker: MIA
segments.en: Like what?

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: Well, she found these articles from the 1950s about how relationships between children and their parents, or between the public and people like bank managers or the police were shifting. [[ ]]

segments.speaker: MIA
segments.en: Interesting. And did you have any practical problems to overcome?

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: Well, in the final rehearsal everything was going fine until the last scene – what’s where the doctor’s first patient appears on stage on his own.

segments.speaker: MIA
segments.en: The one in the wheelchair?

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: Yes, and he had this really long speech, with the stage all dark except for one spotlight – and then that stuck somehow so it was shining on the wrong side of the stage [[ ]] ... but anyway we got that fixed, thank goodness.

segments.speaker: MIA
segments.en: Yes, it was fine on the night. ———————–

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: But while you’re here, Mia. I wanted to ask you about the year abroad option. Would you recommend doing that?

segments.speaker: MIA
segments.en: Yes, definitely. It’s a fantastic chance to study in another country for a year.

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: I think I’d like to do it, but it looks very competitive – there’s only a limited number of places.

segments.speaker: MIA
segments.en: Yes, so next year when you are in the second year of the course, you need to work really hard in all your theatre studies modules. Only students with good marks get places – you have to prove that you know your subject really well. [[ ]]

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: Right. So how did you choose where to go?

segments.speaker: MIA
segments.en: Well, I decided I wanted a programme that would fit in with what I wanted to do after I graduate, so I looked for a university with emphasis on acting rather than directing for example. It depends on you [[ ]] . Then about six months before you go, you have to email the scheme coordinator with your top three choices. I had a friend who missed the deadline and didn’t get her first choice, so you do need to get a move on at that stage [[ ]] . You’ll find that certain places are very popular with everyone.

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: And don’t you have to write a personal statement at that stage?

segments.speaker: MIA
segments.en: Yes.

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: Right. I’ll get some of the final year students to give me some tips [[ ]] ... maybe see if I can read what they wrote.

segments.speaker: MIA
segments.en: I think that’s a very good idea. I don’t mind showing you what I did. And while you’re abroad don’t make the mistake I made. I got so involved I forgot all about making arrangements for when I came back here for the final year. Make sure you stay in touch so they know your choices for the optional modules [[ ]] . You don’t want to miss out doing your preferred specialisms.

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: Right.

SECTION 3
Questions 21-30
THEATRE STUDIES COURSE
Choose the correct letter A, B or C.
Questions:
    Q Num: 21
    Text: What helped Rob to prepare to play the character of a doctor?
    Options:
        the stories his grandfather told him.
        the times when he watched his grandfather working.
        the way he imagined his grandfather at work.
    Q Num: 22
    Text: In the play's first scene, the boredom of village life was suggested by
    Options:
        repetition of words and phrases.
        scenery painted in dull colours.
        long pauses within conversations.
    Q Num: 23
    Text: What has Rob learned about himself through working in a group?
    Options:
        He likes to have clear guidelines.
        He copes well with stress.
        He thinks he is a good leader.
    Q Num: 24
    Text: To support the production, research material was used which described
    Options:
        political developments.
        changing social attitudes.
        economic transformations.
    Q Num: 25
    Text: What problem did the students overcome in the final rehearsal?
    Options:
        one person forgetting their words.
        an equipment failure.
        the injury of one character.
Year abroad option
What action is needed for the following stages in doing the 'year abroad' option?
